text:
Ravi: FYI saw a weird client repro today where streaming chunks from two hedged conns interleaved and the client got duplicate tokens.
Nina: Ugh. Do you have the trace id?
Ravi: trace=tr-9a3, small-token payloads, hedging enabled (hedge=1, fastfail=40ms). Primary resumed with token 42, hedge resumed with token 43, then primary emitted a late chunk labeled 43 again.
Tom: Curious  our resume token assignment can be racy if we reuse tokens before old writers are fully retired.
Liza: Current model: resume token = monotonic offset but generated by the backend; gateway stamps it when emitting. If a hedge picks up a newer offset while primary still has buffered frames we lose ordering.
Nina: Quick thought: enforce a per-request "handoff lease" that the gateway grants to a single emitter. New candidates request lease; gateway only flips lease when prior holder acks drain or lease timeout.
Tom: That would guarantee single-writer at the gateway level. But hedging benefits drop since new writer might wait instead of emitting immediately.
Ravi: Tradeoff accepted for correctness on streaming routes. We can make it configurable per-route. Default for chat-like routes should be "ordered"; for fire-and-forget endpoints allow optimistic mode.
Liza: Implementation sketch: when conn B says "ready(offsetX)" gateway checks if lease held by A. If held, gateway sends A a "soft-drain" request with short grace_ms. A flushes up to offsetX then returns "drained(offsetY)". Gateway then atomically flips lease to B. If A fails to drain within grace_ms, gateway forcibly revoke and mark gap alerts.

Tom: Need to handle crash scenarios: if holder disappears mid-drain, lease TTL in control plane must expire and gateway must ensure tokens already emitted are durable so resume is safe. Suggest persist lease state in control-plane KV with short TTL and lease epoch.

Nina: Also billing: ensure we attribute emitted tokens to the final accepted writer only. If A emitted some bytes then B emits overlapping offsets, we should dedupe billing or attribute to whichever offset range each connection actually sent. Gateway needs to report per-conn offsets to billing svc.

Ravi: Observability additions: lease_acquired, lease_revoked, drain_duration_ms, overlap_detected, billing_overlap_events. Add trace tags for conn_id and lease_epoch.

Liza: Config additions per route: swap_mode = [atomic|optimistic], grace_ms, per_req_buffer_bytes, lease_ttl_ms. atomic = gate keeps single-writer semantics, optimistic = allow concurrent emit (legacy behavior).

Tom: For optimistic mode we should at least attach conn_id meta to resume tokens in the gateway telemetry (not leaked to clients) so we can diagnose reordering without changing client protocol.

Nina: Testing plan: unit harness that simulates interleavings, e2e with chaos injector (kill conns mid-drain), and perf bench with 5k rps small-chunk to measure latency impact of atomic mode.

Ravi: Action items: 1) spike lease datastore shim (Tom) 2) gateway handshake + soft-drain code (Liza) 3) router config flags + docs (Nina) 4) telemetry + billing hooks (Ravi)

Tom: I'll open a spike PR and include a microbenchmark. Expect ~1 week.

deploy-bot: Reminder: register infra RFC if you plan control-plane changes that modify lease schema. https://redwood-internal/infra/rfcs :robot_face: 

Liza: Agree. Also will add a small integration test asserting no out-of-order chunk delivery for atomic mode.

Nina: One more nuance: client-side reconnection. If client reconnects and we handed off lease, we must ensure resume token semantics still work. Gate should record last-ack-offset per-request in store so new client resumes cleanly.

Ravi: Good call. Include last-ack-offset persistence in the spike.

Tom: Cool. Posting spike link when ready. Thanks everyone.

Nina: lgtm.
